# JSON XML Editor (PayloadParser): instructions for Claude

This file loads in every Claude Code session, so it stays short. Detailed project knowledge lives in
`docs/sdlc/` and is read when a task needs it. The two files below are loaded every time.

@docs/sdlc/00-project-overview.md

## Build, run and test

- Run locally: `./mvnw spring-boot:run` → http://localhost:8085 (port from `PORT`, default 8085)
- All tests: `./mvnw test`
- One test class: `./mvnw test -Dtest=SdlcGeneratorServiceTest`
- Package the jar: `./mvnw package` (add `-DskipTests` to skip tests)
- Production front-end build (minify + obfuscate `static/` into `frontend-build/dist/`, used by the Dockerfile):
  `cd frontend-build && node build.mjs`
- The running app serves static files from `target/classes/static`. After editing files in
  `src/main/resources/static`, refresh them with `./mvnw -q process-resources` (delete `target/classes/static`
  first if old files linger). After moving SDLC template files, delete `target/classes/sdlc-templates` too.
- No formatter or linter is configured.

## How to work in this project

- Before changing code, read the code around the change and the relevant doc in `docs/sdlc/`, and follow the
  patterns already used. Check "Where new code goes" in the folder-structure doc before creating files.
- Keep each change focused on the task. Don't refactor, rename or reformat unrelated code.
- After changing code, run the build and the relevant tests and show the result. Never claim something works
  without having run it; if you couldn't run it, say so.
- Ask when a requirement is unclear or two docs disagree, instead of guessing.
- Never read, print or commit secrets (`.env` files, keys, passwords, tokens). If a task needs one, ask.
- When you state facts about libraries, APIs or standards, follow `.claude/rules/research-and-sources.md`.

## Project docs

Sections marked `<!-- FILL: … -->` are not filled in yet; `<!-- INFERRED: … -->` means Claude wrote it and a
person hasn't confirmed it. How to treat them: `.claude/rules/how-to-use-sdlc-docs.md`.

| Doc | Read it when |

| `docs/sdlc/03-architecture.md` | Before a change that touches more than one module |
| `docs/sdlc/04-decisions/` | Before changing something an ADR decided |

| `docs/sdlc/research/` | Before researching a topic, check whether it was researched already |

## Commands

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `/sdlc-init` | Reads the project, fills empty doc sections it can work out, asks about the rest |
| `/sdlc-status` | Shows which docs are filled, inferred or still empty, and what to do next |
| `/analyze-structure` | Maps the folders and updates `docs/sdlc/01-folder-structure.md` |
| `/research <question>` | Researches a question in the code and on the web; writes a report with sources |
| `/explain <area>` | Explains how part of the code works, with file:line references |
| `/sync-docs [since]` | Updates the docs after code changes so they don't drift |
| `/requirements <feature>` | Writes user stories with Given/When/Then acceptance criteria |
| `/design <REQ or change>` | Designs the change and records important choices as ADRs |
| `/implement <story>` | Builds it with tests and proves it by running them |
| `/write-tests <target>` | Adds missing tests to existing code |
| `/refactor <target>` | Restructures code without changing behaviour, tests before and after each step |
| `/fix-bug <bug>` | Reproduces, finds the root cause, fixes with a test |
| `/review-changes [target]` | Reviews uncommitted changes, a branch or a PR, ranked by severity |
| `/commit` | Checks the changes for secrets and debug code, writes the message, commits after you confirm |
| `/open-pr` | Writes the pull request description and creates it after you confirm |
| `/check-dependencies` | Outdated and vulnerable libraries, with upgrade risk |
| `/prepare-release [version]` | Writes the changelog entry and release notes |
| `/test-plan <REQ>` | Risk-based test plan for a feature or release |
| `/test-cases <story>` | Test cases from the acceptance criteria, with traceability |
| `/automate-tests <cases>` | Turns test cases into automated tests and runs them |
| `/run-tests [suite]` | Runs tests, classifies every failure, records the results |
| `/bug-report <problem>` | Reproducible bug report with evidence, severity and duplicate check |
| `/regression [changes]` | Picks the tests a change could break, runs them, writes a checklist |
| `/performance-check <target>` | Finds what makes code or a page slow, ranked by impact, with fixes |
| `/accessibility-check <target>` | Checks UI against WCAG 2.2 AA and lists issues with fixes |

Developer flow: `/requirements` → `/design` → `/implement` → `/review-changes` → `/commit` → `/open-pr` →
`/prepare-release`. Use `/sync-docs` after merging.

Tester flow: `/test-plan` → `/test-cases` → `/automate-tests` → `/run-tests` → `/bug-report` → `/regression`.
Testing docs: `docs/sdlc/testing/` (strategy, plans, cases, bugs, runs, traceability matrix).

Agents Claude hands work to: `researcher`, `test-runner`, `architect`, `debugger`, `code-reviewer`,
`security-reviewer`, `test-designer`, `test-automation`, `bug-triager`, `performance-analyst`. Use
`test-runner` for builds and test runs to keep long output out of the conversation.

## Project-specific rules

- No comments in front-end code (HTML, CSS, JavaScript under `src/main/resources/static`).
- When a page's CSS or JS file changes, bump its `?v=` query string in every page that loads it, so browsers
  don't serve the old cached version.
- Browser-only tools must not send the user's data to the server; keep processing client-side.
- The server runs on Render's free tier with little memory: avoid heavy server-side processing and large
  in-memory caches.
- The Claude Code SDLC generator's templates and generation logic stay on the server (`sdlc/` package,
  `src/main/resources/sdlc-templates`). Never move templates or rendering into front-end code.
- SDLC templates are stored as `CLAUDE.md.tmpl` and `dot-claude/` so they don't load as instructions in this
  repository; keep that naming.
- New tool pages need: a route in `ViewHandler`, an entry in `static/js/tools-list.js`, links in the header
  and footer where relevant, a sitemap entry, and SEO limits of 60 characters for titles and 160 for
  descriptions.
- Page copy should read naturally, written for people rather than keyword-stuffed.
